newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power drops on warmer weather forecast.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power drops on warmer weather forecast.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) fell Tuesday on forecasts of warmer weather in the state over the next several days, industry sources said.

Temperatures through Texas were expected to reach maximums in the 40s degrees Fahrenheit area in north Texas and into the high 50s in south Texas Wednesday, a significant rise from the below-freezing temperatures of Monday.

Thursday temperatures in Texas were expected to be near normal, although a cooling trend was expected Friday and Saturday through the state with temperatures falling to five to 10 degrees below normal.

ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Wednesday delivery was discussed at $37.00-41.00 from $46.00-50.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) on Monday for Tuesday delivery, the brokers and marketers said.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Wednesday delivery was talked at $24.50-28.50 from Monday discussion notionally assessed at $23.00-25.00 per MWh, the sources said.
February ERCOT power was said to have fallen to $31.50-32.50 from $35.50-36.00 per MWh on Monday.
One trader said August ERCOT peak power was talked at $25.50-26.00 per MWh.
